title: Badge body — /badge/{node_id}.json and /badge/cert/{cert_id}.json (shields.io endpoint response)
description:
The badge body a README embeds, in the shields.io ENDPOINT schema. Two rules govern it and both are about honesty rather than looks.

(1) A STALE BADGE MUST NEVER KEEP ASSERTING REGISTRATION (WEB-085). `suspended`, `quit` and `delisted` repositories all render the neutral form — label unchanged, message 'status: see registry', colour lightgrey — and the edge route serves the neutral form even against a still-cached artifact whenever the index meta's delist set contradicts it (FS10-032). An unknown node_id answers 200 with `isError: true` and 'not registered', because shields renders errors from bodies, not from 404s (FS10-033).

(2) NO MONEY FIGURE BEFORE THE LEDGER. The default message is mechanism copy ('registered'); a charity band may render only after the first franc actually moves, and the band thresholds and visual design are an open decision (URS §21 OPEN-11, VS-24, MKT-042).

SCHEMA-VERSION NOTE: `schemaVersion` here is shields.io's own literal `1`, which happens to satisfy the FS-00 §6.2 requirement that every artifact carry a schema version. This artifact deliberately carries NO `generatedAt` field: the body must remain a valid shields endpoint response, so freshness travels in the `ETag` and `Last-Modified` headers instead (FS10-003).

THE CERTIFICATE BADGE (1.1.0, pre-release; ops decision D115, slice P13b): the edge also answers `/badge/cert/{cert_id}.json` in this shape, computed from the certificate's published record (`certificate-record.v1`) on each cache miss and stored nowhere, beside the same certificate's SVG badges. It names no person, no project and no figure: its message is one of the fixed words below, followed for a crediting state by the certificate's period as a year or a year range. A certificate that is not on the plane, or whose record was erased, answers 200 with `isError: true` and `not found`, exactly as an unknown repository does. An organisation's certificate is governed by the claim kit (1.2.0, pre-release; ops decision D115's dated note of 2026-10-13T07:01Z item 1): a LISTED company's Entitlement, shown in full and logged as a credited contributor's certificate must be, says the kit's badge text after the label, kit-1 `variants.supporter.badge` ("Purpose Source · {lane} Entitlement · {status}"), with the word `verified` where the kit says valid, because no picture says "valid". Every other organisation's certificate (an unlisted company, a waiver, a sponsor or another supporter variant, a person's supporter certificate, a revoked or superseded Entitlement, an Entitlement with any other display or no log position) and a steward's have no badge words, and their badge routes answer 404.

schemaVersion.description: shields.io endpoint schema version. Must be the literal 1.

label.description: Fixed left-hand text. Constant across every state so a reader's eye tracks the right-hand message, and so a neutral badge is visibly the SAME badge rather than a different one.

message.description: Right-hand text. Canonical values on a REPOSITORY badge: `registered` (every registered repository that is not suspended, whether or not its admins have claimed it: the platform's internal states `detected` and `verified`, ops decision D82 item 5), `status: see registry` (suspended/quit/delisted, as before), `not registered` (unknown id). A money band may appear only post-first-franc (OPEN-11). *(Amended 2026-09-30, D82 item 5: `registered` said "(verified)"; no value was added.)* Canonical values on a CERTIFICATE badge (1.1.0): `credited {years}` (a contributor's certificate shown in full whose status is `valid`, or `expired` by the clock, as a participation record is once its period is over), `verified {years}` (the same, recorded status-only), `revoked`, `updated, see new` (superseded), `not found` (no such certificate, or an erased one; `isError: true`), and `test` (a certificate signed with a non-production key, served off production only). `{years}` is the period's year, or its first and last year joined by an en dash (`2025–2026`). On a LISTED COMPANY's certificate badge (1.2.0): `{lane} Entitlement · verified` (a `supporter.entitlement` certificate shown in full and logged whose status is `valid`) and `{lane} Entitlement · expired` (the same, expired by the clock), where `{lane}` is `Project`, `Portfolio` or `Pass`, the lane its scope names; such a certificate signed with a non-production key says `test`, and an erased one `not found`, as every certificate does. No message names the organisation or states a band, an amount or a period.

color.description: Canonical values on a repository badge: `brightgreen` (registered), `lightgrey` (neutral), `inactive` (unknown id). On a certificate badge (1.1.0) the colour is the one its SVG badge draws, from the site's palette: `#1d5c3c` (credited, verified), `#8a1f1f` (revoked), `#45505c` (updated, see new; not found), `#7a4d06` (test); on a listed company's (1.2.0), `#1d5c3c` for an Entitlement in force and `#45505c` for an expired one.

isError.description: True only for the unknown-node_id response, which is still served with HTTP 200 (FS10-033), and for a certificate badge's `not found` (1.1.0).

cacheSeconds.description: Shields' own cache hint. Kept consistent with the edge cache policy: s-maxage 3600, stale-while-revalidate 24 h, stale-if-error 7 days (FS10-033, INF-15).
